measure.code: measure.{u} {α : Sort u} (f : α → ℕ) : WellFoundedRelation α
measure.fullDefinition: abbrev measure {α : Sort u} (f : α → Nat) : WellFoundedRelation α :=   invImage f Nat.lt_wfRel
measure.description: A function mapping elements from a type to natural numbers defines a well-founded relation on that type.

WellFoundedRelation.wf.code: WellFoundedRelation.wf.{u} {α : Sort u} [self : WellFoundedRelation α] : WellFounded WellFoundedRelation.rel
WellFoundedRelation.wf.description: Every well-founded relation is guaranteed to be well-founded in the sense of having no infinite descending sequences.

WellFounded.fix.code:
WellFounded.fix.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {C : α → Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop} (hwf : WellFounded r)
  (F : (x : α) → ((y : α) → r y x → C y) → C x) (x : α) : C x
WellFounded.fix.fullDefinition: noncomputable def fix (hwf : WellFounded r) (F : ∀ x, (∀ y, r y x → C y) → C x) (x : α) : C x :=   fixF F x (apply hwf x)
WellFounded.fix.description: A function for defining a unique fixed point in a well-founded context allows for constructing a value based on prior values related through a specified relation.

WellFoundedRelation.mk.code: WellFoundedRelation.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} (rel : α → α → Prop) (wf : WellFounded rel) : WellFoundedRelation α
WellFoundedRelation.mk.description: A well-founded relation can be constructed from a given relation that is known to be well-founded.

Acc.intro.code: Acc.intro.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (x : α) (h : ∀ (y : α), r y x → Acc r y) : Acc r x
Acc.intro.comment:
A value is accessible if for all `y` such that `r y x`, `y` is also accessible.
Note that if there exists no `y` such that `r y x`, then `x` is accessible. Such an `x` is called a
_base case_.
Acc.intro.description: A value is considered accessible if all related values are also accessible under a given relation, establishing a basis for cases with no related values.

WellFounded.intro.code: WellFounded.intro.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), Acc r a) : WellFounded r
WellFounded.intro.description: A relation is considered well-founded if every element associated with it is accessible.

WellFounded.induction.code:
WellFounded.induction.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (hwf : WellFounded r) {C : α → Prop} (a : α)
  (h : ∀ (x : α), (∀ (y : α), r y x → C y) → C x) : C a
WellFounded.induction.description: A property can be proven for an element in a well-founded relation by showing it holds for all related elements, thereby concluding it holds for the specific element in question.

WellFounded.fix_eq.code:
WellFounded.fix_eq.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {C : α → Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop} (hwf : WellFounded r)
  (F : (x : α) → ((y : α) → r y x → C y) → C x) (x : α) : hwf.fix F x = F x fun y x => hwf.fix F y
WellFounded.fix_eq.description: The fixed point of a well-founded relation with a specified function equals the result of applying that function to its argument and the fixed points of all related arguments.

Prod.Lex.left.code:
Prod.Lex.left.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {ra : α → α → Prop} {rb : β → β → Prop} {a₁ : α} (b₁ : β) {a₂ : α}
  (b₂ : β) (h : ra a₁ a₂) : Prod.Lex ra rb (a₁, b₁) (a₂, b₂)
Prod.Lex.left.description: If one element is related to another via a specified relation, then the pair consisting of that element and a second element is also related to another pair in a lexicographic order defined by those relations.

Prod.Lex.right.code:
Prod.Lex.right.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {ra : α → α → Prop} {rb : β → β → Prop} (a : α) {b₁ b₂ : β}
  (h : rb b₁ b₂) : Prod.Lex ra rb (a, b₁) (a, b₂)
Prod.Lex.right.description: If two elements in a second type are related according to a specified relation, then their ordered pairs with a constant element from the first type are also related under the lexicographic order defined on pairs.

PSigma.Lex.left.code:
PSigma.Lex.left.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop} {s : (a : α) → β a → β a → Prop} {a₁ : α}
  (b₁ : β a₁) {a₂ : α} (b₂ : β a₂) : r a₁ a₂ → PSigma.Lex r s ⟨a₁, b₁⟩ ⟨a₂, b₂⟩
PSigma.Lex.left.description: A pair of values is lexicographically ordered according to a specified relation if the first components are related by that relation and any corresponding second components satisfy a designated ordering.

PSigma.Lex.right.code:
PSigma.Lex.right.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop} {s : (a : α) → β a → β a → Prop} (a : α)
  {b₁ b₂ : β a} : s a b₁ b₂ → PSigma.Lex r s ⟨a, b₁⟩ ⟨a, b₂⟩
PSigma.Lex.right.description: If a relation holds between two elements in a dependent type for a fixed first component, then this relation extends to the corresponding elements in the dependent sum type.

WellFounded.apply.code: WellFounded.apply.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (wf : WellFounded r) (a : α) : Acc r a
WellFounded.apply.description: From a well-founded relation, the accessibility of a specified element can be established.

Prod.lex_def.code:
Prod.lex_def.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (r : α → α → Prop) (s : β → β → Prop) {p q : α × β} :
  Prod.Lex r s p q ↔ r p.1 q.1 ∨ p.1 = q.1 ∧ s p.2 q.2
Prod.lex_def.description: A pair of elements is related under the lexicographic order if the first elements are related or if they are equal and the second elements are related.

Acc.recOn.code:
Acc.recOn.{u_1, u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : (a : α) → Acc r a → Sort u_1} :
  {a : α} →
    (t : Acc r a) →
      ((x : α) → (h : ∀ (y : α), r y x → Acc r y) → ((y : α) → (a : r y x) → motive y ⋯) → motive x ⋯) → motive a t
Acc.recOn.fullDefinition: inductive Acc {α : Sort u} (r : α → α → Prop) : α → Prop where   /--   A value is accessible if for all `y` such that `r y x`, `y` is also accessible.   Note that if there exists no `y` such that `r y x`, then `x` is accessible. Such an `x` is called a   _base case_.   -/   | intro (x : α) (h : (y : α) → r y x → Acc r y) : Acc r x
Acc.recOn.description: A recursive function processes accessible values based on a specified motive, allowing for reasoning about each value and its related values within a defined structure.

InvImage.wf.code:
InvImage.wf.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {r : β → β → Prop} (f : α → β) (h : WellFounded r) :
  WellFounded (InvImage r f)
InvImage.wf.description: The image of a well-founded relation under a function remains well-founded.

Subrelation.wf.code: Subrelation.wf.{u} {α : Sort u} {r q : α → α → Prop} (h₁ : Subrelation q r) (h₂ : WellFounded r) : WellFounded q
Subrelation.wf.description: A subrelation of a well-founded relation is also well-founded.

WellFoundedRelation.rel.code: WellFoundedRelation.rel.{u} {α : Sort u} [self : WellFoundedRelation α] : α → α → Prop
WellFoundedRelation.rel.fullDefinition: rel : α → α → Prop   wf  : WellFounded rel
WellFoundedRelation.rel.description: The relation defining a well-founded ordering on a type derives from the well-founded relation over that type.
